originalTitle: Elon Musk's Tesla posts cash burn as capex surges on AI, robotaxi push
simplifiedContent: Here's what you need to know: Tesla, a company run by Elon Musk, spent a lot of money in the last quarter, which means it didn't have as much cash as it would have liked. This happened because the company is investing heavily in new technologies like artificial intelligence and self-driving taxis. Even though Tesla sold more cars than expected and its energy storage business did well, it still lost $1.1 billion in cash. Investors are watching to see how Tesla's investments in new areas will pay off, especially since the car market is getting more competitive. This matters because investors want to know if Tesla's big spending will lead to future growth and success.

originalTitle: Google quarterly cloud revenue growth beats expectations
simplifiedContent: Google's cloud business had a very strong quarter, with revenue growing 82% due to high demand from large companies for artificial intelligence (AI) services. This growth was better than expected and helped alleviate worries about the large amounts Google's parent company, Alphabet, is spending on AI. Google's search business is also doing well, with more advertisers using its AI features. The only downside is that Google's own AI model development is behind schedule. Overall, Google's strong cloud and search businesses are positive signs for the company.

originalTitle: US stocks today: S&P 500, Nasdaq close lower amid mixed show by tech stocks ahead of earnings
simplifiedContent: Here's what happened in the US stock market today: the S&P 500 and Nasdaq, which are like big lists of important stocks, ended the day with lower values. This happened because some tech stocks, like software companies, did poorly, while others, like chip companies, did well. Investors are being careful because some big companies, like Alphabet and Tesla, are about to report how they're doing, and this can affect the market. Rising oil prices and global tensions are also making investors a bit nervous, which is making the market unpredictable. This mix of good and bad news is making it hard to predict what will happen next in the market.

originalTitle: Yen Rebound Ebbs After Brief Rally on Outlook for BOJ Rate Hikes
simplifiedContent: The value of the Japanese yen recently went down to a very low point, with one dollar being able to buy more than 163 yen, which is the lowest it has been in over 35 years. However, the yen then started to recover and gain some of its value back. This change happened because some people think the Bank of Japan, which is like a bank for the country, might raise interest rates faster than expected. The yen's value went up a bit because of this possibility, but it's still uncertain what will happen next. This matters because changes in the yen's value can affect the economy and investments in Japan.

originalTitle: Two-year yields hit 17-month high on oil surge, Fed fears
simplifiedContent: The interest rate on a type of US government bond that matures in two years has reached its highest level in 17 months. This happened because of a surge in oil prices and concerns about what the Federal Reserve (the US central bank) might do next. When oil prices go up, it can lead to inflation, which might prompt the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates. As a result, investors are selling their bonds, which drives up the yield, or interest rate, on those bonds. This change in interest rates can affect the overall direction of the stock market and the economy.

originalTitle: Gold firms to two-week peak on softer dollar, Fed outlook in focus
simplifiedContent: The price of gold has reached its highest point in two weeks. This happened because the value of the US dollar has gone down, which makes gold more attractive to buy. People are also waiting to see what the Federal Reserve (the central bank of the US) will do next, which is affecting the price of gold. This matters because it can impact the investments of people who own gold or are thinking of buying it. The change in gold's price is important for investors to know about as they consider their next moves.
